title: Agents — goals (registry + convergence)
description: ADR-102 §Convergence is a number (homelab#209, supersedes IL-G04's unbuilt gauge). Series: github-exporter's goal walk (goal_* — one series family per task/goal issue, descendants resolved from the NATIVE sub-issue tree at any depth, never label-derived) joined to the pushgateway's agent_run_cost_usd by the goal_spent_usd recording rule. Doubles as the goal REGISTRY: what goals ran, with what verdicts, at what cost — a query instead of archaeology. Closed goals age out after ~30d; older ones stay queryable in Prometheus, just not on this page.

panels.title: Open goals
panels.description: Goals currently OPEN across every repo the exporter walks. A goal is a task/goal issue with a machine-parsed Budget: line (ADR-102).

panels.title: Goal spend in view
panels.description: Σ goal_spent_usd — every run charged to any issue in a visible goal's descendant tree (the goal itself included: its decompose/coordination rounds draw the same budget). All-time per goal, NOT a rolling window.

panels.title: Convergence by stack — 7d sprouts filed minus descendants closed
panels.description: THE convergence number (one tile per stack). >0 = the trees are growing faster than they are being closed out — a goal whose tree grows while its budget drains is visibly diverging. Both operands are per-goal series that always exist together, so the vector match never drops a stack. Sprouts = descendants at depth>=2 (harvest sprouts + the post-launch bucket's children); fixes = delta() of the closed-descendant gauge, not increase(), because that series is a gauge.

panels.title: Goal registry — verdict, budget, burn, tree (row → the goal issue)
panels.description: The registry ADR-102 asks for: every goal in view with its verdict, its Budget: line, what the tree has actually spent, and how the tree is moving. Verdict is a goal/validated|goal/reverted|goal/abandoned label when the claim taxonomy carries one (ADR-102's three terminals) and otherwise the GitHub-native close reason — completed/not_planned — which is all that is knowable today; an open goal reads `open`. A goal with no parsable Budget: line has an EMPTY budget cell, not a zero: unfunded-unknown is not funded-zero. The `key` column (project#goal) exists only to join the six queries — goal numbers repeat across repos.

panels.title: Budget burn — spent ÷ the goal's Budget: line
panels.description: 1.0 = the goal has spent its funding. The launcher's pre-flight gate (Σ spend + live reservations ≤ Budget:) refuses the NEXT child dispatch around here, so a bar at 1.0 is a goal that has stopped being able to dispatch — ADR-102's ABANDONED decision point (refill or close). Goals with no parsable Budget: line are absent from this panel by construction.

panels.title: Open descendants per goal (the burn-down that is supposed to fall)
panels.description: Open issues anywhere in each goal's native sub-issue tree. Flat-or-rising while spend accrues is the divergence shape goal-174 showed for 34h post-close with nothing owning the tree.

panels.title: Sprout inflow vs fix rate (7d), by stack
panels.description: The two curves behind the convergence tile. Inflow = increase(goal_sprouts_filed_total[7d]) — depth>=2 descendants, i.e. review harvests and post-launch bucket children. Fix rate = delta(goal_descendants_closed[7d]). Inflow above fixes for a sustained stretch is a stack filing work faster than its goals absorb it. Caveat: the sprout counter is recomputed each poll from the exporter's issue window, so a sprout aging out of GOAL_ISSUE_WINDOW looks like a counter reset (increase() then undercounts) — goal_tree_truncated says when that window is biting.

panels.title: Descendant tree — every issue charged to a goal (row → per-issue $ drill-down)
panels.description: The membership series goal_spent_usd joins against, shown raw: one row per (goal, descendant, depth), depth 0 being the goal itself. This is what makes the money attributable — and what to look at first when a burn-down number looks wrong. depth>=2 rows are the sprouts.

panels.title: Read honesty — truncated issue windows / goal query support
panels.description: goal_tree_truncated=1 means that repo has more issues than the exporter's GOAL_ISSUE_WINDOW, so a descendant that has not been updated recently can be missing from every count on this page. goal_query_supported=0 means the exporter fell back to its pre-#209 GraphQL query (the goal fields were rejected) and the goal series are ABSENT rather than wrong — PR/review metrics are unaffected either way. A dashboard that hid these would be reporting a partial tree as a whole one.
